Section performance

Build a line. Watch where it backs up.

Add sections, connect their dots, and set dimensions and operating rates in the inspector. Start with an example or build from an empty grid. Run animates items. Step mode pauses automatic pick and pack operations. Advance frame moves time by one selected zone travel interval; the exact seconds are shown. + 60 s advances up to one minute. In Step mode, every source assignment, ready pick and ready packout must be addressed before further time advances; a frame pauses as soon as a new decision appears. Click a tote or use the Items tab to inspect contents and perform manual work.

Layout controls

  • Drag sections to move. Drag from an output dot (L/R/S or A/B) onto an input dot (IN or RE) to connect. Multiple feeds can share an input. Links can filter cases, empty/partial/full totes, or orders.
  • Click a section or link to edit. Delete removes the selection; R rotates a section. Curves and transfers have a Left-hand / Right-hand setting in the inspector; switching hand mirrors the turn and keeps connections attached. Ctrl+Z undoes layout edits. Shift/Ctrl-click toggles sections and connections; Shift-drag empty grid selects both inside a box. Select sections of one type to bulk edit their shared attributes, or select only connections to edit shared link settings. Drag a selected group to move it. Ctrl+A selects all sections and connections; Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V copy and paste sections with their internal links; Ctrl+D duplicates; Ctrl+X cuts. Display names are preserved and routing IDs remain unique. Drag empty grid to pan; scroll to zoom.
  • Physical parameters and connection edits reset the simulation. Routing IDs, destination selections, manual tote actions, and moving or rotating sections preserve the current run. Layouts save automatically in this browser; JSON moves them between computers.

What the model does

ComponentBehavior
Transportation / curveTravel time from length ÷ speed. Entire belt stops when its lead item is blocked; maintains item spacing.
AccumulationItems advance independently, limited by physical pitch or zone length. Stops propagate as the buffer fills.
90° / bidirectional transferSingle item at a time. Residence is the greater of travel time or cycle time. 90° transfer has a left/right divert (L/R) and straight-through (S) exit. Bidirectional T has left/right exits; + adds straight-through (S). All exits share the configured transfer cycle.
MergeConfigurable N numbered inputs and one shared output. Opportunity serves earliest-ready input; Priority serves the highest-ranked ready input; Round robin rotates after each accepted item and skips inputs without eligible ready items. Inputs share entry spacing and the output release interval.
DiverterWeighted, next available, preferred/secondary or full-tote conditional dispatch.
GravityIndependent item movement using your assumed effective speed; slope/friction physics are not calculated.
Source / empty tote inductDeterministic arrivals at items/min. Blocked arrivals remain in an external queue, so demand is never silently dropped.
Pick stationConfigurable tote capacity, with one picker processing totes in arrival order. Adds configured fill percentage, capped at 100%. Tote dimensions remain unchanged.
Packing stationAccepts totes at or above the minimum fill and converts each to one order carton after the pack cycle. Carton dimensions are configurable; an empty tote return is not emitted.
DischargeOne service slot, configurable seconds/item and recurring downtime.

Tote contents retain labeled fill contributions from each pick, with timestamps and station IDs, rather than individual SKU quantities. Each tote carries a destination. Give transfers a unique routing ID and destination exit (L/R/S), choose the first divert when inducting empties, and choose the next destination after partial picking. Destination routing follows the shortest connected path and overrides weighted dispatch. A destination transfer sends the tote through its configured exit, then targets the assigned pick station when an itinerary is present; otherwise it clears the destination. The next pick sets a new destination. Connect pick outputs to optional RE inputs on accumulation to return totes into an open zone. Blocked zones hold returning totes at the station. Each RE connection can require a consecutive empty-zone gap before release; the default for new return links is two zones, including the receiving zone plus adjacent upstream space. Near the inlet, the gap extends downstream. The check uses complete tote footprints, and simultaneous returns recheck space after each insertion. RE connections can also monitor any conveyor or pick/pack station, using either occupancy or lead tote contents fill, and require that reading to be at or below / at or above a threshold. Both enabled gates must pass before release. Tote sources offer independent per-area probabilities and an ordered itinerary; manual mode requires review before induction and confirmation of every ready pick. Frame duration is zone length ÷ belt speed, so blocked items may move less than one zone. Work order matrices generate bounded integer pick quantities and station visits, with seeded randomness. Choose Each visited station for independent per-station pick limits and separate station-count limits; total order picks are their sum. Random visits use area probabilities conditioned on the station limits, which can change observed percentages. Preview shows both distributions. Existing layouts retain Entire order and balanced sampling until switched. Random range allows every feasible quantity between the limits while meeting the average; Min/max only is an endpoint stress mix. A station visit completes all pick units assigned there. In balanced sampling, percentages totaling 100% mean exactly one visit per tote; 200% means two. Random visits can span the separate station limits. Order fill means completed picks divided by assigned picks, not physical tote volume. No SKU or inventory model is included. Order cartons and totes remain distinct item types.

Connection extenders

Use the 3×3 Connection extender to bend connection arrows and clean up a schematic. It has one input and one output, in S (straight), L (left) or R (right) variants. Its dots sit at grid-cell centers; rotating it keeps them on the grid. It adds no travel time, storage or processing cycle. Chains of extenders behave as a single connection: all link filters apply, and the final receiving input, capacity and reinduction gates are preserved. Extenders do not change route distance or create a buffer. A disconnected or cyclic chain holds items at its physical feeder. Use conveyors when a connecting run should add physical travel or storage.

Node trends

Open Trends, select any node or follow the selected graph section, and choose metrics from the checkbox dropdown. Rates, material totals, occupancy, fill, operating state, picks, packing, routing exits, reinductions and tote timing are available where applicable. Separate plots preserve units and keep configured capacity separate from measured rates. Display zoom changes the rendered size of all charts, labels and legends. Fit all shows every selected chart inside the chart viewport; Fit width fills its width. Enlarge the display to read labels and use scrollbars to move through it. Expand charts opens a larger viewer. Time zoom magnifies the selected time range; Time position moves through it. Value zoom magnifies each value axis; Value position moves up/down that axis. Fit visible data shows small changes, while Include zero preserves the baseline. Reset zoom restores the full range. Overlay scales each series to its own peak so different units can be compared by shape. Points have exact-value tooltips. CSV exports selected series; Interactive HTML report includes every node and retained sample with working selectors for offline review and printing. Open full report pauses the run and shows the selected charts. Sampling starts at one simulated second; long histories are progressively thinned to bound memory. Reset or physical edits start fresh trend history. Wait excludes planned movement and work, while residence includes them. Completed-tote timing uses cumulative releases; held timing measures current items.

Multi-input merges

Two-input merges use a 3×3 square with IN1 and IN2 centered in the top and bottom cells of the input-side column, and the output centered in the opposite column. Three inputs fit the same block; larger input counts add rows so numbered ports remain on the grid. Set the number of inputs, connect one conveyor to each dot, and choose Opportunity, Priority or Round robin. A single ready input can feed; the merge does not require simultaneous arrivals. Priority ranks every input and never waits for an empty higher-priority feed. Round robin advances its scan after every accepted case/tote/order and skips unready inputs, alternating when two feeds remain ready. Opportunity uses oldest continuous readiness, breaking ties by input number. Inputs are eligible only if their head item is ready to release and its material filter / destination permits that connection. Capacity, downtime, item spacing and release timing still apply. Input counters and the next round-robin scan are shown in the inspector. Old shared-IN links are assigned distinct numbered inputs when imported.

Conditional diverts and preferred directions

At a 90° transfer, bidirectional transfer or divert, enable Full tote? and select YES / NO exits. YES means a 100% tote, with all assigned work-order picks completed. Other items can use a specified NO exit or normal destination routing. A full-tote lane may wait when blocked or use the secondary exit. Select Preferred exit → secondary if blocked as the dispatch rule to prioritize an exit for normal traffic. Preferred is rechecked when the item is ready to leave; secondary is used only if preferred has no usable downstream entry space. Filters, receiving capacity, downtime and reinduction gates all apply. If both are blocked, the tote waits. Assigned destinations are preserved: alternate lanes must connect to that destination, even if their paths are longer or recirculate through this same transfer before taking its primary exit on a later lap. Fallback checks entry space at the receiving section; if the primary lane can still accept a tote, the tote uses that lane. If both entries are blocked, it waits. The inspector shows full-tote release / fallback counts, and item history records each conditional decision.

Bypass busy pick branches

At a mainline transfer or divert, enable Pick bypass → Continue mainline and retry next lap. Set Pick branch direction to its station feeder and Mainline bypass direction to the recirculation line. Auto monitoring uses the tote’s assigned pick station; choose an explicit station for fixed routing to a divert. Assigned totes bypass if the feeder entry is blocked or the pick station has reached its tote capacity or is stopped. They retain their pending picks and destination. When space opens on a later lap, the branch is tried again. Both entries blocked means wait. The bypass must reconnect to the same pick branch; routes that lose the assigned station are rejected. This setting applies only to totes destined for that branch; completed totes retain their full-tote lane rules.

Work order matrices

Open Order matrix, select your source, and set each station’s percentage of totes needing picks. These percentages may total more than 100%. Choose average picks per tote, hard minimum/maximum pick quantities, station limits, and an order-size variability setting. Generate equal station percentages from an average stop count, then edit individual rows. In Entire order mode, extra-pick weights allocate units beyond the first pick at each selected station. Preview checks observed percentages and order sizes without consuming the simulation sequence; use the same seed to repeat a run. Routing sorts selected stations by connected distance, searches for a complete itinerary, and holds failed orders at their source. The Orders report distinguishes assigned demand from completed work. Set additional seconds per pick at each station to make order quantities affect service time. Step mode requires reviewing every generated work order and confirming every ready pick and packout. An order must finish all assigned picks before packing.

Run videos

Click Record MP4, choose 720p or 1080p and the entire layout, current editor view, or Tote-cam, then Start recording. Tote-cam lets you choose a starting tote and close-up zoom; a tote selected in the editor is preselected. It follows the same tote-derived order through packing until final discharge, then waits for the first newly inducted tote. Only the tracked tote shows all label details in the recording; other totes have compact number plates. Your editor label preference is preserved, and the camera zoom adjusts to keep the tracked tote’s details visible. Use Run, Pause and Advance frame normally. The red REC button stops and prepares an MP4 download with moving items, the simulation clock, queues and measured output. Videos are silent and record real elapsed time at up to 30 fps; faster playback compresses more simulated time into the video. Paused time is included. Keep the tab visible for smooth recording. Recording ends at 10 minutes or 256 MiB. Your browser must support MP4 recording or H.264 encoding; unsupported browsers show a message. Everything is processed locally in your browser.

Panels, tote labels and reports

Drag the dividers beside the left/right panels or above the bottom metrics/report to resize. Focus a divider and use arrow keys for keyboard resizing; double-click it or use Reset panels to restore defaults. Panel sizes and tote label preferences are saved in this browser. Compact nameplates show the tote number. Recirculating totes have red tote and nameplate borders, including in MP4 recordings. The mark begins after a successful pick bypass, a secondary exit onto a return loop, or revisiting a section without reaching a workstation/discharge. It clears on taking the original preferred exit or reaching a pick station, pack station or discharge. Waiting at a blocked entry alone does not mark recirculation. Hover a nameplate to see its completion percentage/bar and remaining destination list using routing IDs, including pick diverts and the assigned packout. Completed picks drop off the list. Always Show All keeps both details visible; Always show completion percentage keeps the bar and percentage visible; Always show destination keeps the routing ID list visible. Hover in any mode shows all details. Off hides nameplates. Unassigned packout/discharge is described as any eligible destination. Timeline records chronological blocking episodes with their start/end simulated timestamps, duration, first receiving blocker, gate conditions, tote IDs and peak queue/occupancy. Filter short events, then Generate report to print/save as PDF or download a standalone printable HTML. CSV on the Timeline tab exports every matching retained event. Overlapping entries can reflect a downstream block propagating upstream; reasons are model observations. The log resets with the simulation and retains up to 50,000 events; omission is reported if the limit is reached. Connection clicks work along the full curve at any zoom. Copy on connections copies their shared settings, and Paste applies those settings to selected existing connections.

Rates and diagnosis

Belt ceiling = speed ÷ (item length + gap); accumulation also respects zone length. Mixed item sizes consume their actual space. Section capacity estimates use the largest source item for a conservative comparison. Transfers and discharge also obey their cycle limits. Measured throughput, occupancy, blocked time, active time, and starvation come from the running model.

A high blocked percentage points to a downstream constraint. A busy section with upstream waiting is a candidate constraint. The bottleneck report separates these observations; run long enough for the system to fill and settle.

This is a seeded, first-pass flow model with a 0.05-second timestep. It does not emulate vendor PLC/WCS logic, acceleration, sensor locations, slug release, contact forces, or equipment reliability distributions. Link travel time is zero: add a conveyor to model a connecting run. Cases and empty totes share downstream equipment unless you route them separately.

Record a run

Record the layout, moving totes, simulation clock and throughput as a silent MP4. Recording follows real elapsed time at 30 frames/second; simulation playback speed controls how much simulated time appears. Run, Pause and manual step actions are included.

Select a tote in the editor before opening this dialog, or choose one above. Tote-cam centers on that tote through picking, packing and final discharge, then follows the first newly inducted tote. It holds the last position while waiting. Only the tracked tote shows all label details in the recording; other totes have compact number plates. Your editor label preference is preserved. Zoom backs off when needed to keep the tracked tote’s details in frame.

Start recording, then run or step the simulation. Stop to prepare the download. Pausing the simulation keeps recording. Maximum recording: 10 minutes or 256 MiB. MP4 encoding depends on your browser; unsupported browsers show a message.
